description: The bar chart presents the average number of likes for posts grouped by a “Most similar group of posts” category defined by degree ranges. The horizontal axis contains five categorical bins labeled (0,90], (90,180], (180,270], (270,360], and (360,450], shown left to right in that order, with labels rotated diagonally; no explicit sorting beyond this sequence is indicated. The vertical axis is labeled “Avg. Like #” and uses a linear numeric scale spanning roughly 400 up to a little above 600, with visible tick labels at 400, 450, 500, 550, and 600 (regular 50-unit intervals). Each category is represented by a single light-blue bar with a thin dark outline and a vertical error bar (black line with caps) centered on the bar top: (0,90] is approximately 600 likes, (90,180] is approximately 567 likes, (180,270] is approximately 572 likes, (270,360] is approximately 595 likes, and (360,450] is approximately 590 likes. The error bars vary in length across categories, with approximate ranges of about ±15–20 for (0,90], ±18–20 for (90,180], ±25–30 for (180,270], ±25–30 for (270,360], and ±30–35 for (360,450]. No legend, stacking, grouping within categories, or special visual emphasis beyond the error bars is shown.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the average number of likes, represented by the vertical axis labeled 'Avg. Like #,' for different categories of post groups. The horizontal axis contains categories labeled as ranges in degrees: (0,90], (90,180], (180,270], (270,360], and (360,450]. The vertical axis is on a linear scale with values ranging from 400 to 600, marked in increments of 50. Each bar represents a specific group range and is colored light blue. The bars corresponding to the categories (0,90] and (360,450] show the highest average likes, consistently exceeding 600 likes, while the (90,180] category shows the lowest average likes, with values below 500. The error bars indicate variability or uncertainty in the average like values, with the (180,270] category showing the smallest variability compared to others.
